rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials went off track on every track (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.24 on the oval, 0.17 on the s-bend and 0.12 on the slalom, with 1 to 2 line-loss events and steering oscillation of 0.10 to 0.14. The robot is failing from instability, not from speed alone. With kp = 2.5 and weights of +/-2, the turn command can reach about 5 units (about 1750 PWM of differential), which is far too aggressive. The result is overshoot and oscillation that carry the robot off the tape. Changes: (1) kp lowered from 2.5 to 1.5 so the largest turn is about 3 units, which should cut the overshoot. (2) kd raised from 0.2 to 0.6 to damp the oscillation that remains. (3) ki set to 0 because the integral adds windup and lag on curves and the errors are small. (4) base_speed lowered from 1.5 to 1.3 so the robot has time to correct on the tighter slalom bends. This gives up some speed, so completion within 3 s is less likely, but staying on the line is the first requirement. (5) wheel_track widened from 0.12 to 0.14 m, so each unit of turn produces a gentler change in turn rate. (6) Sensors moved to y = 0.05 m ahead to look a little further down the line, which should reduce lag. Sensor spread, weights, mass and body stay as in iteration 0 to keep the comparison clean. Expected result: several trials should now stay on track on the oval and s-bend, with steering_oscillation below 0.08 and at least some finishes on the oval. The slalom may still leave the track. Hypotheses to test next: (H1) lower kp removes the off-track failures, with progress rising above 0.5 on the oval; (H2) kd of 0.6 cuts steering_oscillation by about half; (H3) base_speed of 1.3 is too slow to finish within 3 s, so a later iteration must raise speed once stability holds. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and control_effort, to check whether the change in kp and kd is what made the difference.
